title: Size the caps to the corpus, regenerate the artifact, pin both directions
description: The decided remedy: raise every implicated channel's maxInlineBytes to a value derived from the committed corpus, keep StateBloatError as a guard against genuinely runaway writes, regenerate the artifact and the state audit, take a MINOR graphVersion bump with a changelog entry, and pin each cap two-directionally against the corpus so that neither shrinking nor inflating one can happen silently.

successCriteria.description: src/pge/topology/coding.graph.ts declares, for every channel the measurement implicates, a maxInlineBytes at least the corpus maximum for that channel, and .bober/topology/coding.json is regenerated from it via `pge dump`.
graphVersion takes a MINOR bump and docs/pge-graph.md gains a changelog entry keyed by it, stating which caps moved and the measured basis for each.

`pge dump --check`, `pge validate --mode full`, `pge docs --check`, `pge diff --require-version-bump` and `pge audit-state` followed by `git diff --exit-code` all pass against the regenerated artifact and the regenerated state audit.

A test pins each cap two-directionally against the committed corpus: lowering a cap below its corpus maximum FAILS, and raising a cap with no corpus payload justifying it FAILS. Both directions proven by mutation.
A negative control proves StateBloatError still bites: a value above the NEW cap is still rejected and the write is still dropped, so the check was re-sized rather than removed.
The golden dataset still passes unchanged -- a MINOR bump does not invalidate cases, and no golden file is edited in this sprint.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green.

nonGoals: Removing or weakening the StateBloatError check.
Adding the specDraft channel, which is sprint 7.

Editing a golden case for any reason OTHER than refreshing the graph.graphVersion stamp after this sprint's MINOR bump. The recapture is authorised ONLY if the diff is exactly that one field per case and nothing else; any other field moving is a stop condition.
stopConditions: The golden dataset fails after the cap change -- stop and report; a MINOR cap bump should not move any recorded artifact, and if it does, that is a defect worth understanding before proceeding.
`pge diff` reports the change as MAJOR rather than MINOR -- stop and reconsider the classification rather than forcing the bump.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and every documentation claim added is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
assumptions: HEADROOM SCHEME (resolves the tension in sc-3-4, designed by the curator, adopt unless you find it wrong): pin each cap as EQUALITY to a pure derived function of the corpus, capForCorpusMax(corpusMax) = the next power of two at or above 2x corpusMax, floored at DEFAULT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES. This satisfies BOTH directions of sc-3-4 because the cap is a FUNCTION of the corpus rather than a literal: lowering below the corpus max and inflating without justification both break the equality. It also absorbs the messages/evaluations resampling drift within a power-of-two bucket. Under it only two caps move: spec 48,097 -> 131,072 and sprintContracts 135,106 -> 524,288; the other eight channels stay at exactly 4,096.

SIZE FROM 48,097, NOT 29,214. Two spec-channel maxima appear in the docs and both are correct: 29,214 is THIS repository's own PGE spec (sprint 1) and 48,097 is the largest of all 52 parsing specs (sprint 2). The cap must accommodate the largest real spec.

pge diff has NO MAJOR/MINOR classifier — verified. src/pge/topology/diff.ts:231-240 exposes only isVersionBumped, a forward-move check. The sprint's MAJOR stop condition is therefore unsatisfiable, and the golden dataset's MAJOR-only integrity check (case-schema.ts:371-377) survives a bump to 1.3.0.

FOUR BLOCKERS OUTSIDE THE ORIGINAL estimatedFiles, verified by the orchestrator — a cap or version change reddens all of them: (a) src/pge/engine/real-workload.test.ts hardcodes 4096 in about seven assertions and byte-compares the committed measurement; (b) src/pge/topology/coding.graph.test.ts:117 pins graphVersion to "1.2.0"; (c) src/pge/topology/docs.test.ts:971 pins changelogVersions to exactly ["1.2.0","1.1.0","1.0.0"] AND its negative control at :975 uses the LITERAL "1.3.0" as its "version the changelog does not mention" fixture — so adding a 1.3.0 changelog entry breaks the very test that guards the pairing, and that fixture must be re-keyed to an unused version; (d) the render fixtures src/pge/topology/__fixtures__/coding.mermaid and coding.dot are byte-pinned on the version header and need regenerating.

The measurement artifact .bober/topology/measurements/real-workload.json is owned by sprint 4, which regenerates it to show the rejections gone. This sprint may need to touch it; if so, keep the change minimal and say so.
generatorNotes: Edit the AUTHORED literal at src/pge/topology/coding.graph.ts:113-190, then regenerate the committed JSON with the pge CLI -- never hand-edit .bober/topology/coding.json, which `pge dump --check` will catch anyway. Pick caps from the corpus with deliberate headroom and say in the code comment what the headroom is for; a cap that exactly equals today's maximum will fail the day a spec grows one field. Keep StateBloatError: the point is to size the guard, not to delete it. Remember the state audit is a committed artifact gated by `pge audit-state` plus `git diff --exit-code` (src/pge/audit-git-gate.test.ts), so regenerate it in the same commit.
evaluatorNotes: Verify the two-directional pin genuinely bites in BOTH directions by mutating it yourself -- lower a cap below corpus max and confirm failure, then raise one arbitrarily and confirm failure. A pin that only catches shrinkage is half a pin. Verify the negative control for StateBloatError by constructing a value above the new cap and confirming the write is dropped and a StateBloatError lands in `rejected`. Confirm .bober/topology/coding.json was regenerated rather than hand-edited by running `pge dump --check` yourself. Confirm the changelog entry states a MEASURED basis per cap, not a round number with no provenance.
completionNote: All 7 criteria met on iteration 2. spec 4,096 -> 131,072 and sprintContracts 4,096 -> 524,288; other eight unchanged. graphVersion 1.3.0 + changelog. Caps pinned as EQUALITY to capForCorpusMax = next power of two at or above 2x corpus max — proven non-tautological by the evaluator's own standalone mutation script in both directions for both channels. StateBloatError re-sized, not removed. 5 golden replay cases recaptured, diff verified as exactly graph.graphVersion and nothing else. In-flight specs excluded from the corpus (keyed on PlanSpecStatus) after the corpus was found to invalidate itself mid-run. Suite 6877/0 failed. MAJOR FINDING carried to sprint 4: with the caps raised the run now reaches the 14-contract fan-out and throws SuperstepLimitExceededError at DEFAULT_MAX_SUPERSTEPS=200 before any terminal node. The byte cap was masking a second wall; the two defects only looked like one symptom.
